claims.claim: Breach of fiduciary duty (loyalty) — affiliate fees and dilution
claims.why: §7.3 eliminates fiduciary duties to the fullest extent permitted; §18-1101(c) permits; pleading it invites dismissal and fee/credibility cost; pushback wants it anyway

claims.claim: Breach of express contract — §5.4 (arm's-length terms; 30-day written disclosure of affiliate transactions)
claims.direct_or_derivative: derivative as to excess fees (company harmed); direct as to the disclosure right

limitations.tolling_argument: fraudulent/contractual concealment — §5.4 disclosure never made; one-page summaries concealed; client learned 2026 → tolling for 2022–2023 fees is arguable but not assured

claims.remedy: disgorgement of excess over market; derivative demand futility (sole interested manager)

claims.claim: Breach of express contract — §6.3 capital call defective
claims.remedy: declaration that no Dilution Event occurred (notice not by certified mail/email; 'working capital and opportunities' arguably not a bona fide stated purpose); restoration to 18%; §9.2 buyout right not triggered

claims.claim: Implied covenant — bad-faith exercise of discretion (fair-value determination of $7.2M vs $14.5M broker indication; call sized and timed to dilute)

valuation_gap.why: §6.3 notice mechanics not followed (text only; no certified mail; email bounced); purpose vague; Manager's 'fair value' $7.2M vs independent $9.8M equity → implied-covenant challenge

strategy: Do not accept $189,100. Send a demand/§6.3 notice-defect letter before Oct 31 reserving rights; books-and-records (§18-305) to complete the fee record; file in Chancery: (1) declaratory relief on the capital call/dilution (direct, strong, cheap to plead); (2) §5.4 contract claim for fee disgorgement (derivative, futility pleaded), with tolling argued for 2022–23; (3) implied covenant as to the valuation. Do NOT plead fiduciary duty. Funding: contingency/litigation funding or a negotiated exit at a number anchored on the $1.76M indication; a negotiated buyout above book is a realistic outcome given limitations and litigation cost.
pushback: pleading a waived claim 'to scare him' risks dismissal and undermines the strong contract claims; Delaware enforces §18-1101(c)
